headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: uptrend holds, price stays soft as Binance reopens

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is still to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is intact, and this kind of phase has historically been when spending to win new and returning users paid back best, especially among active traders. This week calls for applying it carefully: Binance has reopened withdrawals but its fuller reserve report is still due, price is about 5% under its 50-day average, and the mood is fearful, so add spend in small steps, lead with safety and trust rather than hard offers, and speed up only once price wins back about $81,969. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC ($78,172) is about 7% above its 200-day average ($73,171), which is still rising.
Up about 22% over 90 days; about 84% of those days closed above the long-term average.
But price has closed under its 50-day average ($81,969) for 12 days, about 5% below it.
Binance reopened withdrawals with about 2% of assets leaving; Fear & Greed is 37 (fear).
watch: The long-run trend still points up, but price has spent 12 days under its 50-day average and the mood is still fearful. A clean Binance reserve report and a close above $79,750 would steady things, while a close below $77,369 puts the $73,171 average in focus.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds, and the worst of the Binance scare has eased, but prices have not recovered yet. Short term is soft to neutral: Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 12 days, sits about 5% below it and about 10% under its 30-day high, and the mood still reads fear (37 out of 100). Binance reopened withdrawals on all 15 first-phase networks on 1 November and says about $3.64 billion net left, around 2% of its assets, with the flow since slowing (PANews); its fuller reserve report is expected today but was not confirmed at the time of writing. A normal week now swings about $2,926, so a close above $79,750 (top of a typical week's swing) would turn it clearly up, a close below $77,369 (the 30-day low) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy. A clean reserve report would help the mood; until then, keep leading with trust rather than offers.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 22% higher, but the last 30 days are down about 8% and October was one of Bitcoin's weakest Octobers on record (CoinGlass via PANews). Price must win back $81,969 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and it only has room to climb above $86,603 (the 90-day high); while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading. This week brings the US midterm elections on 3 November and the US jobs report on Friday 6 November, and the next Fed meeting is 8 December. Save bigger campaign pushes for that reclaim.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up at a moderate strength. Price is about 7% above its 200-day average and that average is still rising, about 3% over 90 days, though Bitcoin remains 37% below its all-time high. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,171 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,390 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. So far the largest crypto theft on record has not broken this picture, and a close below the 200-day average is what would weaken it, which would be the moment to move budget toward keeping existing users.

items.theme: Binance theft fallout hits altcoins and THORChain
items.why: The Binance attacker sold more than 130 smaller coins on EVM chains for about $279 million in ETH and USDC, according to Lookonchain. THORChain, a cross-chain trading protocol, paused trading after an Ethereum glitch and says its vault is whole again after a user returned 10 ETH. The reports do not give a clear reason for RUNE's fall.
items.marketing_angle: A good education topic: why stolen funds move across chains and what that means for smaller coins.

sources.title: Binance Attacker Dumps Over 130 Altcoins on EVM Chains Alone, Total Value Around $279 Million
THORChain: User Voluntarily Returns 10 ETH, Vault Regains Solvency

items.theme: Pushback against tokenized US stocks grows
items.why: Fifty listed companies, now including Nvidia and Walmart, have objected to their shares trading in token form on the OKX and ICE platform, up from 33 a few days earlier. The platform published the updated list in a public notice.
items.marketing_angle: Keep any tokenized-stock content factual, and do not promise which shares will be available.

Akedo and AWE also fell hard, but the reports do not give a clear reason. Large token releases this week include KITE and MMT, per Token Unlocks.
items.marketing_angle: An education topic for newer users on why small tokens swing more and what a token release is.

items.theme: A run of wallet security scares
items.why: BTCPay Server told operators to shut down after hot wallets on several instances were drained; the cause and losses are not yet disclosed. Solana Mobile said a fake app in its dApp Store asked users for their seed phrase and has been taken down.
items.marketing_angle: Timely hook for account-safety content aimed at existing users.

items.name: COTI
items.update: COTI went live on Uphold, a fiat on-ramp the project says serves more than 10 million users. On 29 Oct the project also took part in Mozilla Festival 2026, a gathering on privacy and digital rights. Both are the project's own statements.

items.name: Genius Terminal
items.update: Genius Terminal announced that part of the revenue from its Genius App will be used to buy GENIUS on the market and burn it permanently, plus new benefits for holders inside the app. PANews reported it on 1 Nov.

sources.title: @GeniusTerminal: new chapter for GENIUS utility (31 Oct)
Genius launches revenue-driven buyback and burn

items.name: Audiera
items.update: Audiera's weekly update says 1.25 million BEAT were burned (32.6 million in total) against weekly revenue of about 128,000 USDT. The price is up about 51% over 7 days; the project's posts do not say why, and its other recent posts are about AI music characters.

items.name: Tagger
items.update: Tagger is up about 64% over 7 days. Its only post this week (28 Oct) describes a plan to bring local and expert knowledge into AI training; no post or news item found explains the rise.

items.name: Re
items.update: Re said it holds no assets on Binance, paused reUSD redemptions on 29 Oct as a precaution after the Binance hack, and resumed them on 30 Oct. PANews also reported Binance Margin removing the RE/USD1 pair on 30 Oct.

sources.title: Binance Margin to remove RE/USD1 and other pairs on 30 Oct

items.name: DODO
items.update: DODO said it is working with Binance to block addresses linked to the hack from using its services, and told market makers and liquidity providers exposed to the affected assets to review their positions.

items.name: Synapse
items.update: Synapse recommended that community members remove their on-chain SYN liquidity while it responds to an incident. The post gives no details, and nothing found links it to the Binance hack.

items.name: Lumia
items.update: Lumia's HyperNode rewards buyback (0.09 USDT per LUMIA) was due to open this week, but the project is allowing extra time because a partner exchange is restoring withdrawals only gradually. USDT payments were announced to begin next week.

items.name: Midnight
items.update: Midnight partnered with Sig Network to bring private transactions to Ethereum apps without bridging or wrapping assets, and demoed its Midnight Passport at TOKEN2049 (29 Oct).

items.name: MegaETH
items.update: MegaETH says its engineers cut zkLogin proof time to about 0.13 seconds (roughly 13 times faster than Sui's current prover, in internal tests), enabling Google sign-in with self-custody in its MOSS wallet. Its October recap also lists a public key ceremony and MNX going live.

items.name: USD.AI
items.update: The CHIP Foundation donated about 128,000 USDai to sUSDai holders under its CHIP Hurdle Rate; the project says holders since 15 Oct earned about 7% APY. It also says it has financed $531 million of GPUs across 20 deals.

items.name: Babylon
items.update: Babylon announced the Bedrock × Babylon vault, which lets native Bitcoin serve as DeFi collateral without wrapping or bridging (details "coming soon"), and refreshed its testnet app for Bitcoin-backed borrowing.

items.name: Espresso
items.update: Espresso's co-founder is due to speak at Hong Kong Fintech Week on 3 Nov about settlement speed for AI agents. The project also published a deep dive on sub-second finality in its HotShot consensus.
